# Volume 3 — Chapter XVII A Letter from Robin

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Girls, snow is starting to fall,” stated Cressy, entering on an evening in November, “and the path through the garden is covered with the most charming tiny crosses and stars. The fact that snowflakes are such truly exquisite objects had never caught my attention until now. A person possesses the time for observing details of that nature when leading the simple life. I thank you all for allowing me the opportunity to experience it. Feeling anxious over a five-cent increase in the price of a pound of butter is actually wonderful.”
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0000 }

“Is that so?” asked Mabel, the one responsible for the family’s financial records.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0001 }

“It has—and your butter is right here. I am becoming rather skilled at shopping. It is more enjoyable than flirting,” Cressy stated seriously.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0002 }

“Prices are rising at a scandalous rate,” Mabel let out a sigh.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0003 }

“Don't worry. Thank goodness we still don't have to pay for air and salvation,” Aunt Euphemia said.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0004 }

“Laughter is the same way,” Nell appended. “It isn't taxed yet, which is fortunate, as every one of you will be laughing shortly. Robin’s letter is what I am about to read to you. Over this last year, his spelling has gotten vastly better, even if apostrophes aren't his strong suit, and he undeniably has a talent for composing an engaging letter. Give this a listen and laugh, prior to us getting down to the evening’s study-grind.”
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0005 }

“Dear Nell,” Robin’s letter began, “I am writing to let you know that everyone here is doing well enough, and I hope you are also in good health. Snow is falling a bit today, and Thirza tells me the old woman up in the sky is dusting her feather mattresses. Is that old woman in the sky married to God, Nell? I would like to know.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0006 }

“Mrs. Sowerby was quite ill, though her health has improved now. The previous week, she tumbled down the steps to the cellar. As she dropped, she clutched the ledge holding every single milk pail and stewpan, causing it to collapse and plummet alongside her, producing a glorious racket. Initially, Thirza believed an earthquake was happening.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0007 }

“A stewpan got completely dented, and Mrs. Sowerby strained her ribs. Following the doctor's arrival, he provided her with liniment for her ribs, yet she failed to comprehend his instructions and swallowed the entire dose instead. Although the doctor remarked that it was miraculous she survived, she suffered no fatal effects, her ribs were healed, and Mrs. Sowerby maintains that doctors possess little knowledge regardless. Nevertheless, repairing the stewpan proved impossible. Thirza was forced to discard it. Thanksgiving occurred during the previous week. Classes were canceled, and a grand feast took place. I consumed mince pie, roast turkey, fruit cake, donuts, cheese, jam, and chocolate cake. Thirza predicted that I would perish, yet I survived. Lucy suffered from earache subsequently, except the location was not her ears but rather her stomach. I experienced no earache whatsoever.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0008 }

“The male teacher who just started instructs us in a humorous way. A week ago, he assigned every boy in the third class a task to compose an essay about our ideal future wives, while the girls had to write about their preferred husbands. Reading our papers caused him to burst into overwhelming laughter. I wrote this one, which I believed you might enjoy viewing.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0009 }

“‘The sort of spouse I’d prefer to Possess.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0010 }

“‘She needs to possess good manners, serve my food punctually, obey my instructions, and remain exceptionally polite toward me at all times. She needs to be fifteen yers old. She needs to treat the poor well, maintain a neat home, display a pleasant disposition, and attend church routinely. She needs to be exceedingly handsome with curly hair. Provided I secure a wife who matches my preferences entirely, I will prove to be an extraordinarily fine husband to her. It is my belief that a woman should be exceptionally good to her spouse. Certain unfortunate women possess no husbands whatsoever.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0011 }

“‘THE END.’”
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0012 }

“I attended Mrs. Isaac Ducketts burial at Pale Sands during the previous week. The spouse of the deceased person experienced genuine sorrow. Mrs. Sowerby claims that the grandfather of Mrs. Duckett took a sheep, yet Thirza contends that we ought not talk badly about deceased individuals. Why ought we not, Nell? I wish to understand. It is fairly secure, is it not?
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0013 }

“The other day, Mrs. Sowerby got terribly angry when I inquired whether she lived during Noah’s era. My intention was not to offend her. I merely desired to find out. Did she, Nell?
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0014 }

“Mr. Pettifer desired to dispose of his hound. Consequently, he suspended him once, yet he revived and darted toward the barn as Mr. Pettifer dug his grave, which led him to suspend him once more, and he remained deceased on that occasion. Mr. Pettifer employs a new worker. He is extremely clumsy. Mr. Pettifer remarks that he possesses left-handed traits in both of his feet. Mr. Pembroke’s farmhand is slothful. Mrs. Pembroke asserts this, though Mr. Pembroke states that he is not precisely slothful, merely believing it is simpler to supplicate for items than to labor to attain them.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0015 }

“The prize pig belonging to Mrs. Gorham Pullen, which she spoke of so frequently, perished from a fit. According to Mrs. Sowerby, it was divine punishment for her vanity. However, my opinion is that the pig suffered unfairly. Milty Gammon was ill recently. A foul-tasting medicine was prescribed to him by the physician. I proposed to swallow it in his place if he paid me twenty-five cents, but those Boulters display such stinginess. Milty stated he preferred swallowing it on his own to keep his cash. When I inquired of Mrs. Gammon regarding the way one should proceed to capture a husband, she became extremely angry and replied that she did not know, as she had never pursued men.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0016 }

“The hall will be repainted by the B.V.I.S. They are sick of its blue color.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0017 }

“Yesterday evening, the new minister came over for tea. Three slices of pie were eaten by him. Mrs. Sowerby would term me piggy if I performed such an action. Furthermore, his eating was quick with large bites taken, something Thirza constantly instructs me against doing. What allows ministers to perform actions forbidden to boys? That is what I wish to learn.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0018 }

“There is no additional news from me. Accept these six kisses. xxxxxx. One is sent by Lucy. This is the one from her. x.
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0019 }

“Your loving friend DAVID FARROW”
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0020 }

“P.S. Nell, I want to know, who was the father of the devil?”
{: #nw-v03-c17-p0021 }
